# Plain class terminal Void/void bridges

Owned Java inputs represent a final ordinary class with two abstract ancestors,
an inherited method formal and a closed wildcard interface contract. Encoding
changes only the typed entry names and original forwarding bridge flags; it
checks every Code byte and descriptor before and after each edit.

The independent caller and harness are compiled once before encoding. Seven
routes compare parent/interface dispatch, direct calls, reflection and method
handles for two receivers, null receivers, long boundaries, nullable arguments,
prefix effects and exceptions. The typed method allocates its terminal failure
only after its private prefix returns. Source method names, bridge flags and
bridge parameter reflection are the only reported differences.

The runner checks all DEX and rebuilt classes and methods, original Signature
and Exceptions metadata, and unchanged input/harness/dependency bytes. The
`--dependency-parents` profile consumes Api, Entry, Base and Middle through an
unchanged JAR. Flag and generic scope mutations preserve instruction bytes;
an independent javac input must reject an incompatible wildcard override.
